thread:
Alex S: customer reports repeated 429s during Dedicated scale-up window. says app spikes then requests queue and errors for ~30-90s then recovers. attaching their timeline and a few logs they pasted.

Priya G: thanks. which customer / workspace? any correlation with min_replicas config?

Alex S: cust: fastcart-prod (acct 8743). Dedicated pool: us-west-2-dedicated-4 (pinned to a nv24 instance family). min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, headroom=0.2. spikes to 150 rps. they say autoscaler took ~70s to spin new replicas and kube attach stalled. here's snippet they sent:
```
2026-03-15T14:06:10Z INFO request accept id=... status=queued
2026-03-15T14:06:12Z WARN scaleup: desired=6 current=2 provisioning=0
2026-03-15T14:06:30Z ERROR http 429 path=/v1/generate token=redacted
2026-03-15T14:07:25Z INFO attach complete instance=i-0abcd
2026-03-15T14:07:40Z INFO ready replicas=6
```

Mateo R: curious that provisioning=0 while desired=6. could be instance quota or IAM attach throttling. can we check cloud provider api errors around that time?

oncall-bot: @eng-infra paging oncall due to provider API 403:quota at 2026-03-15T14:06:15Z

Jing L: I pulled the provider events for that pool. there are repeated 429/503 from the provider's attach API between 14:06:05 and 14:07:20. error: "RateLimitExceeded" then "ResourceAttachThrottled". looks like noisy neighbor or region-level throttle.

Priya G: so autoscaler requested instances but cloud blocked attach; autoscaler kept desired=6 because it sees demand, but actual provisioning remained 0. that matches 429s to the customer until attach finished. any reason we couldn't fallback to a cheaper fallback pool or capacity tier?

Alex S: their routing policy pins to that dedicated pool for data isolation. fallback policy is disabled for this customer (enterprise setting).

Mateo R: two things to investigate: 1) whether our backoff logic in the provisioning controller is too aggressive (we might wait longer than necessary on attach throttles), 2) whether we should surface provider attach throttles as a warning to customers earlier (and maybe return 202 queued instead of 429).

Jing L: repro notes: I replayed a scaled-up test in staging and intentionally hit provider attach throttle emulation. observed our controller does exponential backoff but initial retries are spaced ~12s apart which can add up. also our KV warmup actor only runs once instance is attached; if attach is slow, requests pile up and the runtime returns 429 until we have enough ready replicas.

Priya G: can we patch the controller to 1) surface intermediate "provisioning" state to the API (client sees queued with ETA) and 2) reduce first-backoff to 2-4s for attach throttles? both would reduce customer-facing 429 window.

Mateo R: agree. also add an optional soft-fallback for enterprise customers: allow routing to an opaque fallback pool within same region but with an audit log and customer opt-in. not default.

Alex S: customer asks for mitigation now — they want our support team to temporarily increase min_replicas to 4 for the pool while they run a campaign. can we do that quickly?

Jing L: I can update min_replicas for that pool, will need 2-3m to apply and warm caches. note: won't avoid attach throttles if provider is saturated but reduces delta provisioning.

Mateo R: also recommend we trigger a one-off pre-provision (create spare warm instances) so the attach time is zero for next burst. ops-bot: creating prewarm job pool=us-west-2-dedicated-4 count=4 requested_by=Mateo R

ops-bot: prewarm job accepted id=prewarm-1918002345-1 ETA ~180s

Alex S: good — I'll tell the customer. after that can we follow up with infra to add attach-throttle metrics to the console and an alert when provider attach error rate > 5% for 1m? they want SLA explanations.

Jing L: will add metrics and a plain-English blurb for console explaining provider-level throttles vs platform autoscaling.

Priya G: follow-ups: - engineering ticket to reduce initial backoff for attach-type errors (ENG-7123) - product ticket for fallback policy UI toggle for enterprise pools (PRD-456) - ops runbook entry to prewarm on marketing campaigns (OPS-198)

Alex S: thanks all. customer ok with temporary min_replicas bump and prewarm. will close the escalation after we confirm next scale event is handled. :thumbsup:
